perplexity.description:
The album The Life Aquatic With Steve Zissou (Original Soundtrack), released in 2004 by Hollywood Records, is a curated collection of eclectic tracks blending electronic, rock, and cinematic music styles. It serves as the soundtrack to Wes Anderson's film of the same name and features a distinctive mix of original compositions by Mark Mothersbaugh, instrumental pieces by Sven Libaek originally from a 1970s Australian TV documentary, and reinterpretations of David Bowie songs performed by Brazilian musician Seu Jorge. The soundtrack also includes classic rock and new wave tracks such as Devo's "Gut Feeling" and The Stooges' "Search and Destroy," both connected to Bowie through production.

Musically, the album is notable for its quirky, atmospheric tone that complements the film's whimsical and adventurous narrative. The inclusion of Seu Jorge's Portuguese-language Bowie covers adds a unique cultural layer and emotional depth, distinguishing this soundtrack from typical film scores. This soundtrack occupies a special place in the discographies of the contributing artists, particularly Mothersbaugh, known for his work with Devo and film scoring, and Seu Jorge, whose performances gained significant attention through this project. Critically, the album was well-received for its inventive and cohesive blend of genres and for enhancing the film's storytelling, though it is more celebrated as a companion piece to the movie rather than a standalone commercial hit.

The soundtrack runs approximately 33 minutes and was originally released on December 14, 2004. It has since become a cult favorite among fans of Wes Anderson's films and soundtrack collectors, appreciated for its artistic curation and the seamless integration of diverse musical elements under the Hollywood Records label.
